title: Maximum Erasure Value
statement:
`nums` is an array of positive integers. You erase one non-empty contiguous block `nums[l..r]` whose values are all distinct (no value occurs twice inside it), and your score is the sum of the erased values.

Return the highest score you can reach.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every start and extending until a value repeats is correct but O(n²). Notice that if `nums[l..r]` has distinct values, so does every block inside it, and because all values are positive, a longer valid block always scores at least as much as the blocks it contains. So for each right end we only care about the longest valid block ending there, and its left end never moves backwards as the right end advances. That is a sliding window with a set of the values inside it.

## Approach

1. Keep `seen` (values in the window), `left` (window start), `windowSum` and `best`.
2. For each `right`, while `nums[right]` is already in `seen`, drop `nums[left]` from the set and the sum and move `left` forward.
3. Add `nums[right]` to the set and the sum; the window `nums[left..right]` is now valid.
4. Update `best` with `windowSum` and return `best` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4, 2, 4, 5, 6]`. Right ends 0 and 1 give windows `[4]` and `[4, 2]`, so `best = 6`. At `right = 2` the value `4` is already in `seen`, so `4` leaves (`windowSum = 2`, `left = 1`) and the new `4` joins: window `[2, 4]`, sum `6`. Then `5` and `6` join without conflicts: `[2, 4, 5]` sums to `11` and `[2, 4, 5, 6]` to `17`, so the answer is `17`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index enters the window once and leaves at most once.
- Space: O(n): the set holds at most the window's values.

## Pitfalls

- Shrink with a `while`, not an `if`: the repeated value may sit several places after `left`.
- Remove the left value from both `seen` and `windowSum`; forgetting either one corrupts the window.
- Maximise the sum, not the length; here they agree only because every value is positive.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | values currently inside the window |
| `left`, `right` | first and last index of the window |
| `windowSum` | sum of `nums[left..right]` |
| `best` | highest window sum found so far |

narration.2: The set records which values are inside the current window.
narration.4: Running sum of the values in the window, kept up to date as it moves.
narration.5: No block has been scored yet.
narration.7: Grow the window one value at a time on the right.
narration.8: If the new value is already in the window, the window must shrink from the left.
narration.11: ...and move the start of the window past it.
narration.13: The new value is now unique in the window, so add it to the set.
narration.14: Add it to the window's sum as well.
narration.15: The window nums[left..right] is valid; keep its sum if it is the best so far.
narration.17: Every right end was tried with its longest valid window, so best is the answer.
